explanation: Count every distinct string, then keep those whose count is strictly greater than streamLength/k. Cross-multiplication preserves the strict threshold without rounding.
timeComplexity: O(n) expected dictionary operations, plus character hashing: count every stream element once, then inspect at most n distinct keys once.
spaceComplexity: O(u) entries, where u is the number of distinct strings, plus output; each distinct value has one exact counter.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: The dictionary stores the exact frequency of every input string. A frequency count exceeds n/k exactly when count×k>n for positive k, so the final filter retains precisely the required strings without integer-division rounding. Each dictionary key is emitted at most once.
walkthrough: For k=3 and stream ["a","b","a","c","a","b","d"], the length is 7. Counts are a:3, b:2, c:1, d:1. Only a passes count×3>7, so return ["a"].
edgeCases: The threshold is strict: a count equal to n/k is excluded.
An empty stream returns no strings.
Output contains distinct strings in arbitrary order.
